repo_notes.content: Treat the repository's own docs as the source of truth and link to them instead of restating them: docs/architecture/decisions.md (decisions), docs/roadmap.md (what is delivered vs planned), specs/ (journey requirements), docs/install/ and docs/operate/ (installing, running and recovering), docs/maintainers/releasing.md (what a release ships and the release steps). Where an exact command, version or file name matters, cite the canonical doc.
Describe what exists on the default branch. The roadmap and decision record separate delivered work from planned, deferred and candidate work; never present planned or deferred work as implemented.
Names: the product is Your Space; the command is your-space; the npm package is @your-space-ai/cli; the release images are your-space-server, your-space-web and your-space-runtime on GHCR.
Never include secret values, tokens or private keys, and do not describe a maintainer's personal machines or accounts. Signing secrets are referenced only by name.

pages.title: Kit Links
pages.purpose: Reviewing an app from its kit's link, read from public GitHub, and kit files given to the server command. There is no kit directory. The GitHub connection (journey 015): a read-only fine-grained token the owner pastes on the GitHub page or gives to the github server command, stored encrypted under the data key and moved on key rotation. A kit, or the Compose file it pins, that public GitHub doesn't show is read again through it, with the commits and contents APIs; the review labels each private file and names another repository the kit reads, and the installed app records how each file was read. Its optional image token, a classic token with only read:packages, signs the engine in to ghcr.io through the runtime manager (X-Registry-Auth) for images GHCR won't show anonymously.

pages.title: Knowledge Bases
pages.purpose: Knowledge bases (journey 014): the knowledge_base and app_knowledge_base tables, the kit's knowledge field, the runtime manager's labelled ys-knowledge volumes and their setup container, the mounts the Docker adapter adds to an app's interface service, and why removing an app or deleting its data never deletes one. Then their two-way sync with Google Drive: the google_connection and knowledge_sync tables, the server's own OAuth sign-in with the operator's client (state, PKCE, the token encrypted with the data key and moved when it changes), the stock rclone rcd container the runtime manager runs for each synced knowledge base (runtime/src/sync.ts: hardened, mounting only its own knowledge base and state, as rclone writes through symbolic links, its remote control on a Unix socket in its own folder of the ys-sync volume only the server mounts whole, the sync's own Squid for Google's hosts only), and the server driving each over its socket (server/src/apps/knowledge-sync.ts, rclone.ts, bisync.ts): remotes created in rclone's memory with config/create, the timer that runs each knowledge base about once a minute in its own turn, side by side, the restart of an rclone past the two-hour limit or that stopped answering, the job kept on the knowledge_sync row so a result outlives a server restart, the safety stops, the resync it runs itself to finish an interrupted run (once for each interruption, never past a missing marker), Resync and confirmed deletions, conflict copies and backups, and the browser tests' fixture remote (YS_E2E_SYNC_FIXTURE).

pages.title: CI, Release and Packaging
pages.purpose: The CI workflows, the release workflows (Release draft, images, CLI, install test, macOS build and signing, publish) and Canary, which publishes every push to main through them as a canary build. Release publish also points the Alpha channel's feed, the rolling alpha prerelease, at each published release (deploy/alpha-feed.sh), and Canary uploads its channel.json. Mac canary (canary-macos.yml) packages the newest canary build once a day, signs and notarizes its update ZIPs in the macos-canary environment, and adds them with canary-mac.yml to the canary prerelease (deploy/mac-canary-version.sh, deploy/mac-canary-publish.sh). Point to docs/maintainers/releasing.md for what a release ships, the release steps, canary and Mac canary builds, and signing.
